cards.subject: An early pope of the first century, half-length, in a simple deep-red chasuble of antique bell shape over a white tunic, with a plain narrow white wool pallium marked with small dark crosses; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed. With his left hand he rests a dark iron ship's anchor upright against his shoulder, its ring near his cheek; in his right hand a small green martyr's palm. Behind him the Roman harbour of Ostia at the mouth of the Tiber: a stone lighthouse on the mole, a few moored merchant ships with furled square sails, warehouses of brick, and a calm blue-green sea under a clear morning sky. Keep the harbour and ships inside the arched window.
cards.face: A man of about sixty with a diamond-shaped face — a narrow forehead and a narrow, firm chin, broadest at high, prominent cheekbones; a strong, high-bridged aquiline Roman nose; deep-set, dark, thoughtful eyes under straight black brows flecked with grey; a thin, firm mouth; close-cropped black hair receding at the temples and greying above the ears; a short, close-trimmed black beard following the line of the jaw, grizzled at the chin; a calm, attentive gaze slightly to one side.
cards.basis: No likeness survives; the tradition shows him in the pallium with the anchor of his legendary drowning in the Black Sea. The Roman features and short grizzled beard are our choice, set against the city's harbour, to keep him apart from the other early popes.

cards.subject: A Syrian monk-priest of the eighth century, half-length, turned three-quarters, in a dark plum-purple monastic mantle over an ochre-gold tunic, his head wrapped in the white Arab head-cloth crossed with thin black stripes that Byzantine painters give him, falling to the shoulders. In his left hand a long, unrolled blank parchment scroll (no writing on it); in his right a reed pen lifted from a small ink-horn. Beside him on a ledge a small icon of the Mother of God with the Child. Behind him the Great Lavra of Mar Saba clinging to the cliffs of the Kidron gorge in the Judaean desert: honey-coloured stone walls, towers and cells stepped down the rock face, a pale dome, bare ochre hills and a hot, clear sky. Keep the monastery inside the arched window.
cards.face: A Levantine man of about sixty-five with a warm olive complexion and a long, narrow face — a high, lined forehead, a long, thin nose with a high bridge curving slightly at the tip, heavy-lidded, almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under dark, gently sloping brows, lean cheeks under fine cheekbones, a narrow chin hidden in the beard and a small mouth; a long, wavy, iron-grey beard falling in soft strands to the breast and a grey moustache; a grave, gentle, contemplative gaze lowered to the scroll.
cards.basis: No likeness from life survives; the Athonite fresco on Wikipedia shows the Byzantine type: a long, lean face, a long wavy grey-white beard and the striped white head-cloth, writing on a scroll. The card keeps that type, iron-grey rather than white, with the olive complexion of a Damascene Arab and Mar Saba, where he lived and wrote.

cards.subject: An archbishop of the twelfth century, half-length, standing calmly, in a deep-red chasuble of full medieval cut over a white alb, a white wool pallium with small dark crosses over his shoulders, and a white mitre with gold bands; in his left hand a gilt crozier, in his right a closed Gospel book held to his breast. No sword, no wound, no violence. Behind him the Romanesque cathedral of Canterbury as it stood in 1170: pale Caen-stone walls, round arches and a massive square central tower, with the roofs of the city and green Kentish fields beyond under a soft winter sky. Keep the cathedral inside the arched window.
cards.face: A tall, spare man of about fifty with a pale complexion and a long, narrow, well-formed face — a high forehead, a long, fine nose with a gently arched bridge, bright, lively dark eyes under dark, straight brows, lean cheeks with a faint colour high on the cheekbones, a firm, narrow chin and a finely shaped, closed mouth; clean-shaven; dark-brown hair, just touched with grey at the temples, cut short around the tonsure beneath the mitre; a steady, resolute, serene gaze straight ahead.
cards.basis: William FitzStephen, his clerk and biographer, describes him as unusually tall and slender, pale, dark-haired, with a long nose and well-formed features; the card follows that. The clean-shaven face follows the twelfth-century British Library miniature (Cotton MS Claudius B II), and the vestments are an archbishop's with the pallium.

cards.subject: An early pope of the fourth century, half-length, in a simple, full chasuble of warm brick-red over a white tunic, a plain white wool pallium falling straight down the front; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed. He holds a large closed Gospel book bound in gold against his breast with both hands, as in the old Roman fresco. Behind him Mount Soracte north of Rome, a long lone limestone ridge rising from green, rolling Tiber-valley countryside, with a small stone hermitage near its summit, olive groves at its foot and a pale, clear winter sky. Keep the mountain inside the arched window.
cards.face: A man of about sixty-five with a long, narrow face tapering to a small, rounded chin — a smooth, high forehead, very large, wide-open almond-shaped dark eyes under high, finely arched brows, a long, thin, perfectly straight nose, smooth cheeks without prominent cheekbones, a small, closed mouth; white hair cut in a neat round clerical ring (the crown shaven); a short, neat, pointed white beard and a thin white moustache; a calm, wide-eyed, gentle gaze straight ahead.
cards.basis: The eighth-century fresco in Santa Maria Antiqua (Wikipedia lead image) shows him frontal, with a long face, very large eyes, a long straight nose, a tonsure and a short pointed beard, holding a jewelled book in a red chasuble and pallium; the card follows it, aged to the end of his twenty-one-year reign. Soracte is where the legend has him hiding during the persecution.

cards.subject: A Roman boy of about fourteen, half-length, in a knee-length white wool tunic with a narrow red stripe at the edge and a short deep-green cloak fastened at the right shoulder with a small round bronze brooch. In his right hand he holds a green martyr's palm upright; his left hand holds a small closed book to his breast. Behind him the Janiculum hill above Rome along the Via Aurelia: tall umbrella pines and cypresses, a low Roman tomb by the road, and beyond, the Tiber and the roofs and domes of the ancient city in the soft light of a spring morning. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
cards.face: A boy of fourteen, visibly a boy and not a young man, with a round face still holding childhood fullness — a smooth, rounded forehead, round, soft cheeks, a short, straight nose with a small rounded tip, large, round dark-brown eyes under straight, thick dark brows, a small dimpled chin and a small mouth with the faint hint of a smile; a light olive, sun-warmed Mediterranean complexion; thick, dark-brown hair in short, tight curls close to the head; no beard; a brave, candid gaze lifted a little upward.
cards.basis: The traditional Passio makes him a Phrygian orphan brought to Rome and beheaded at fourteen on the Via Aurelia; later statues such as the one in Barcelona Cathedral (Wikipedia lead image) show a curly-haired boy in a tunic and cloak with a book and palm. The card follows those, not the medieval soldier type.

cards.subject: An early pope of the third century, half-length, in a simple deep-green bell-shaped chasuble over a plain white tunic and a white wool pallium with small dark crosses; NO tiara, NO mitre, bare-headed. His right hand is raised in blessing; in his left a green martyr's palm and a small closed book. Behind him Trastevere on the right bank of the Tiber in the third century: a modest house-church of brick with a tiled roof among humble workshops and houses, a stone well-head in the small square before it, the river and the Aventine hill beyond, under a warm autumn sky. Keep the scene inside the arched window.
cards.face: A stocky, broad-shouldered man of about fifty-five with a wide, rectangular face and a heavy, fleshy jaw on a thick neck — a low, broad forehead, a broad nose with a wide, flat bridge, small, shrewd, kindly hazel eyes set deep under a heavy brow with thick, straight black-and-grey brows, full cheeks, a wide, generous mouth; thick, straight, coarse hair of black mixed with grey, cropped short and combed forward in a blunt Roman fringe low on the brow (NOT bald, no curls); a short, dense, square-trimmed black-and-grey beard close to the face; a frank, warm, direct gaze.
cards.basis: A former slave who rose to be pope; the medallion portrait in the series of popes at St Paul Outside the Walls (Wikipedia lead image, a pre-1823 fresco) shows a broad face and a short, full beard. The card keeps that sturdy, plain build (with a Roman fringe rather than a bald crown, to stay apart from Sixtus II in batch 7), set in Trastevere, where his titulus stood and where tradition places the well of his martyrdom.

cards.subject: A Camaldolese hermit and cardinal of the eleventh century, half-length, in the full white Camaldolese habit and hood with a scarlet cardinal's cape (mozzetta) over his shoulders and a simple gold pectoral cross. In his left hand he holds a closed book; from his right hand hangs a short plain white knotted cord. Behind him the hermitage of Fonte Avellana under Monte Catria in the Apennines: grey stone monastery buildings and a small Romanesque church on a wooded slope, dark beech and fir forest, a limestone peak with snow on it and a clear, cold sky. Keep the mountain and monastery inside the arched window.
cards.face: A lean, ascetic man of about sixty-four with a long face and a craggy, prominent brow ridge — a high, furrowed forehead, deep-set, burning dark eyes looking upward, a long, strong nose with a slight hook, sharp cheekbones over sunken cheeks, thin, tight lips; short, thick, wiry grey hair; a long, narrow, grey beard falling to the breast in wavy, tapering strands, with a full grey moustache; an intense, searching upward gaze.
cards.basis: The marble bust on Wikipedia gives him a long, tapering beard, deep-set eyes raised upward and a lean face; the Catholic tradition shows him as a cardinal with a knotted cord (the discipline). The white habit is that of the Camaldolese hermits at Fonte Avellana, where he was prior.
